title: Blue Gene/L Kernel TLB & Machine Check Interrupts
text: KERNEL data TLB error interrupt, instruction TLB error, and machine check interrupts indicate hardware/MMU translation or cache parity faults on Blue Gene/L compute nodes. Correlate node ID, adjacent RAS events, and recurring exception addresses before diagnosing faulty compute cards.

title: DDR Memory, L1/L2 Cache & ECC Scrubbing Alerts
text: Total corrected DDR errors, L3 EDRAM error, and L1/L2 cache parity exceptions reflect memory subsystem degradation. Single-bit correctable ECC storms often precede uncorrectable double-bit failures. Inspect node error counts and trend intervals with log_stats.

title: Kernel Data Storage & Alignment Interrupts
text: data storage interrupt and alignment exceptions in KERNEL logs typically stem from invalid memory references, null pointer dereferences, or misaligned user/kernel accesses during HPC job execution. Verify whether the failure isolates to one job/node or spans multiple nodes.

title: Application & CIOD / I/O Node Read Failures
text: APP subsystem messages such as ciood / ciod failed to read message prefix, socket errors, or job termination signals indicate I/O daemon communication failures between compute nodes and I/O nodes. Cross-check adjacent network or filesystem timeouts.

title: Torus / Tree Network & LinkCard Failures
text: LINKCARD, torus receiver, and tree network packet/CRC error logs signify interconnect link instability or cable/switch degradation across racks. Check whether multiple nodes on the same midplane report simultaneous link failures.

title: MMCS Control System & Node Discovery
text: MMCS and DISCOVERY events track node booting, block allocation, and hardware inventory discovery. Repeated discovery failures or unreachable service cards indicate control-plane or power/cooling faults rather than user application bugs.

title: HARDWARE & Environmental RAS Monitoring
text: HARDWARE subsystem alerts cover temperature sensors, fan speeds, power supplies, and board voltage rails. Environmental thresholds can trigger automated node shutdowns or cascading kernel interrupts.

title: Kernel Program Interrupts & Illegal Instructions
text: program interrupt: illegal instruction or privileged instruction traps in KERNEL logs occur when a process executes corrupted code, mismatched binaries, or unsupported CPU opcodes. Inspect neighboring stack/register dumps when available.

title: Interpreting BGL Severity Levels (INFO vs ERROR/FATAL)
text: In BGL logs, INFO entries often record routine job/node activity, whereas FATAL, FAILURE, SEVERE, and ERROR entries (normalized to level='error') denote fault events. Always quantify severity distribution via log_stats rather than extrapolating from top-k search results.

title: BGL Evidence Boundaries & Abstention Policy
text: The BGL dataset contains Blue Gene/L supercomputer RAS logs only. It has no Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, HTTP/Nginx, or cloud IAM incidents. When asked about unsupported systems, inspect evidence and abstain with answerable=false.
